newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ sees Albright strengthening ties with US.
newsitem.headline: NZ sees Albright strengthening ties with US.

text.p: New Zealand, keen to build on improving relations with Washington, on Friday welcomed President Bill Clinton's nominations for secretaries of state and defence.
The two countries fell out in the mid-1980s over New Zealand's ban on nuclear-powered and nuclear-armed vessels from entering its territorial waters.

Clinton lifted an earlier freeze on top-level diplomatic ties and last year received Prime Minister Jim Bolger at the White House. However, New Zealand remains suspended from the three-way ANZUS alliance with the United States and Australia.
Caretaker Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said he was confident Madeleine Albright's nomination as Secretary of State would strengthen bilateral ties.
He also welcomed the choices of Senator William Cohen and Anthony Lake as Secretary of Defence and director of central intelligence, respectively.

"It is clear that President Clinton is building a strong national security team for his second term. It's important that the New Zealand government can work with that team, and these nominations are excellent news for New Zealand," McKinnon said.
